result.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
result.summary: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. Training choices changed how many patients had high attack scores, but the patients who ranked highest by risk largely stayed the same across the configurations we tested. Stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort up to threefold, yet largely the same patients remained most at risk across training recipes, architectures and initializations, including foundation models. Therefore, we developed a lightweight screening tool that uses four small models to identify patients with high risk of exposure before production-model training. We also assessed if flagged patients could be protected without removing their data. Privacy screening should become incorporated into data preparation for clinical AI.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在六个临床数据集、四种模态上训练 7,789 个模型，逐患者测量成员推理攻击下的个体暴露风险，发现高风险患者在不同训练配方、架构与初始化间高度稳定，并据此提出用四个小模型在上线前筛查高风险记录的轻量工具。
AI.relevance_reason: 样本级「影响／暴露」分数跨训练配置稳定，以及用小代理模型预先预测大模型上的逐样本属性，可能与 LVR 中的样本级贡献分配与廉价代理筛选有概念联系，但隐私动机与视觉推理相距较远，迁移价值待核查。
